meta.title: What is Frankencoin? A decentralized Swiss franc stablecoin
meta.description: Frankencoin (ZCHF) is a Swiss franc stablecoin issued by smart contracts against on-chain collateral, without a bank, an issuer or a price oracle.

header.title: What is|Frankencoin?
header.subtitle: Frankencoin (ZCHF) is a digital Swiss franc. Every ZCHF is minted by a smart contract against collateral worth more than a franc, locked on-chain where anyone can inspect it. No bank holds reserves and no company issues it.

features.title: A Swiss franc on-chain
features.description: ZCHF tracks CHF, so you can hold, pay and save in francs on Ethereum and seven other chains without a bank account.

features.title: Backing you can check
features.description: Each ZCHF is backed by more than one franc of collateral: BTC, ETH, tokenized gold and shares, all visible on-chain at any time.

features.title: No issuer, no freeze
features.description: Anyone can mint ZCHF against approved collateral. The rules are smart contracts governed by FCS (Frankencoin Shares) holders, and nobody can freeze your balance.

introduction.title: Why the Swiss franc?
introduction.description: The franc is one of the most stable currencies in the world, and most of the people and businesses using Frankencoin earn, spend and account in it. ZCHF gives them a franc they can use in DeFi and in payments without converting to a dollar token first.

introduction.title: No price oracle
introduction.description: Most stablecoins and lending protocols rely on an external price feed to value collateral. Frankencoin does not. Anyone who thinks a position is under-collateralized can challenge it, and an open auction sets the price. That removes the price feed as a single point of failure; the system still carries market, liquidity and smart contract risk like any other protocol.
